title: Comment the clearing batch to the Code Documentation Standard
summary: Legacy code documented to the firm's rules, with a tool showing that no line of code changed
story: Internal Audit's finding DOC-2026-14 says the clearing batch's comments can't be trusted. Priya Nair brings them up to the Code Documentation Standard with NexCODE: the four layers explain each gap, NexCODE writes the comments, and a tool shows that no line of code changed before the change is recorded.

card.about: Documenting legacy code is the first step of modernising it. The clearing batch's comments name a company that no longer exists, describe rounding the code doesn't do, hold a card number and keep dead code. NexCODE assesses each gap against the four layers of rules, then writes the comments to the Code Documentation Standard: the header with the Bank's notices, a purpose comment for every division, section and paragraph, the stale comments put right. A tool shows that no line of code changed and the program still gives the same totals, and the change is recorded with its AI disclosure.
card.scenario: Monday 20 July 2026. Grace Whitfield of Internal Audit raised DOC-2026-14 in June: the clearing batch's comments fail the Code Documentation Standard. The batch's last COBOL maintainer retires at the end of September, and its Java port is in its parallel run. Priya Nair fixes the comments before cut-over, in one comments-only change.

talkTrack: Documenting legacy code is the first step of modernising it. Select the demo: the program and Internal Audit's finding open, and the checks run once; the program still gives the right totals, but the documentation check fails, as the finding says. Assess: NexCODE reads the program against the four layers and explains each gap, the old company in the copyright line, the comment that says truncated where the code rounds, the card number, the dead code, from the standard to the policy to the regulation. Comment it: NexCODE gives the program back with its comments only; the IDE shows the diff, comment lines alone. If NexCODE's copy changed a line of code, a tool put the program's own line back first, and the chat says which. Apply, then run the checks: a tool shows no line of code changed, the program prints the same totals, and the header and every unit are documented. Record the change: a documentation-only change, verified by tool, with the AI disclosure. Point at the card: DOC-008 is a rule in the Bank's own standard.
